headline: Southern Thailand: Mossad was named in two capitals. No case we checked puts Israel there.
context: Anwar told the Dewan Rakyat in 2025 that Mossad targets Malaysia. Sondhi Limthongkul wrote it to Israel's ambassador on 10 September. We checked a dozen documented cases naming Israel in Thailand and Malaysia since 2012.

cards.big: Sondhi Limthongkul's 10 September letter to Israel's ambassador says Mossad spies sit 'scattered' across Thailand. Anwar told Parliament in 2025 that Mossad targets Malaysia.
cards.sub: Neither mentioned the Deep South. Nor does any case we checked, from Fadi al-Batsh's 2018 killing to Pattaya's nominee files.

cards.big: Iranians jailed in Bangkok in 2013 over bombs police said targeted Israeli diplomats. Shalom Avitan jailed in KL in 2025 over six guns meant, he said, for a rival Israeli.
cards.sub: Israel's embassy counts 41 Thai workers killed on 7 October 2023. Thailand's Foreign Ministry counted 32 that month.

cards.big: Sihasak Phuangketkeow said on 27 July Bangkok would ask Malaysia to deny insurgents safe haven. Kelantan police, 2 August: 'no evidence has been presented to us'.
cards.sub: The foreign hand Bangkok named is a putative sanctuary across the Golok, not Israel. Malaysia's RM3.04 billion fence is due by 2029.

cards.big: Fourth Army chief Norathip Poinok called the 51 attacks of 22 August possible retaliation for his sweeps and an 18.7 million baht cash seizure, pending evidence.
cards.sub: Crisis Group in 2017: nationalists, 'no evidence of jihadist inroads'. Prachatai reported the BRN posted 'Patani-Palestine: Unite' in 2023.

cards.big: The Deep South needs no imported villain. It has a 22-year fight over Malay land, language and self-rule, 333 billion baht in Thai border plans, and 5,989 certified dead.
Like blaming a stranger three streets away for the fire while the neighbour is at the door and the wiring report sits unread.
Every case we checked puts Israel in Bangkok, Pattaya, Phuket or Kuala Lumpur. The foreign hand Bangkok pointed at this year is Malaysia. Kelantan police still await the evidence.

revisions: CORRECTED (Stage 3): headline 'The Thai and Malaysian record does not' → 'No case we checked puts Israel there' (bounded to the reviewed corpus; Stage 3 cardinal-sin flag MISLEADING_FRAMING on the universal negative).
CORRECTED (Stage 3): context 'We traced every case on record' → 'We checked a dozen documented cases' (OVERCLAIM on completeness).

CORRECTED (Stage 3): context 'Malaysia's Prime Minister, a Thai protest leader and Thailand's army have each raised a foreign hand' → the army is removed from that sentence; Stage 2 and Stage 3 both flagged that grouping the army line with the Mossad claims implied the army alleged Israel. The Thai request to Malaysia now has its own card (Security), attributed to Sihasak and the Kelantan police chief, both on the record by name.

STRENGTHENED (Stage 5): the Malaysia-as-alleged-sanctuary thread, which Stage 1 v2 left off the cards, is now the Security card and the view card's second sentence. Stage 5's 'cowardice' flag and Stage 2's omission flag agreed; the evidence (Thai PBS 28 Jul; Bernama 2 Aug) supports it as a live, attributed dispute, not a finding.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '41 Thai workers killed' → attributed to Israel's embassy count, with Thailand's Foreign Ministry figure of 32 (as of 28 Oct 2023) beside it.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'a 2026 nominee-land probe from Pattaya to Pai' → 'Pattaya's nominee files' (DSI primary record is Pattaya/Bang Lamung; no DSI record for Pai). Pai dropped from the view card's list.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'Iranians jailed for a 2012 Bangkok plot on its diplomats' → 'over bombs police said targeted its diplomats' (the target is Thai police's stated finding, per Gen Prewpan, not a judicial finding).

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'Norathip tied the 51 attacks ... to his sweeps' → 'called ... possible retaliation ..., pending evidence' (PRD Narathiwat 24 Aug: the link still required investigation and evidence).

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '340 billion baht of Thai security spending' → '333 billion baht in Thai border plans' (Thai Parliamentary Research Office: 333,679.56 million baht under principal southern-border plans FY2004–FY2024; the plans include development, education and welfare, so 'security spending' was wrong). Stage 2's economic flag agreed.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '5,999 certified dead' → '5,989 certified dead' (SBPAC's own August 2025 publication; the 5,999 figure is a media attribution to a later SBPAC cut-off not located as a primary document).
CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'The BRN itself posted' → 'Prachatai reported the BRN posted' (original upload not retrieved).

REPHRASED (Stage 2 racial flag): reframe now names the stated cause of the conflict ('a 22-year fight over Malay land, language and self-rule') alongside the budget and the dead, so the grievance is not reduced to statistics. Wording rests on Crisis Group (nationalists seeking self-determination) and the BRN spokesman's 14 Sep interview (discrimination against language and culture; self-government).

REPHRASED (Stage 2 partisan flag): Anwar's remark is now 'told Parliament ... that Mossad targets Malaysia over Palestine', which is what he said and how he framed it; it is presented as his statement, not as a finding.

REPHRASED (Stage 2 religious flag, partially): Palestine now appears where the record puts it: in Anwar's own stated reason and in the BRN's solidarity video. The flag's wider ask (to characterise why the rumour resonates with Muslim audiences) is declined; see synthesis_notes.
CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'Mossad enters Malaysia's record only by allegation' and 'All three sit in the Klang Valley' → removed (the 2022 abduction is now off the cards; no court record opened).

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'Meta's 2019, 2022 and 2024 reports ... never name Thailand' → removed from cards for length; the Q1 2024 PDF was text-searched in Stage 1 (zero matches) so the claim stands in the brief, but Stage 3 could not retrieve it and the card budget could not carry the qualifier.
CORRECTED (Stage 3): view card 'A foreign hand is an alibi for every domestic one' → replaced with two attributed facts and a kicker that names the party waiting for evidence.

introduced_claims.claim: Sondhi's letter says Mossad spies are in Thailand 'in considerable numbers, scattered' across various points
Sihasak said on 27 July 2026 Thailand would seek Malaysia's cooperation to prevent those involved in violence from using Malaysia as a safe haven
Kelantan police chief Mohd Yusoff Mamat, 2 Aug 2026: no evidence presented; RM3.04 billion border wall/fence due 2029
Avitan told police he was in Malaysia to hunt down a fellow Israeli
Anwar framed the Mossad threat as linked to Malaysia's Palestine stance
SBPAC certified deaths 5,989 (three-party certified cases, to August 2025)
333,679.56 million baht under principal southern-border plans FY2004–FY2024
introduced_claims.primary_source: Thai Parliamentary Research Office report, as opened and cited by Stage 3: https://prt.parliament.go.th/server/api/core/bitstreams/5028cd05-3dcd-430b-804c-384df85e2a4d/content

synthesis_notes: Over-integration decisions. (1) Stage 2 and Stage 5 both said the Malaysia-sanctuary line was buried; Stage 3 said the Stage 1 inference ('the only country it can refer to is Malaysia') was unsupported. All three are right about different things: the inference from the army's wording was unsupported, but the explicit record (Sihasak's request, the Kelantan police reply) exists and names Malaysia. The cards now use the explicit record and drop the inference. (2) Stage 5 wanted the view card to say the rumour is a fusion of Anwar's, Sondhi's and the army's lines; Stage 3 wanted no unsourced rumour at all. The cards say what each man said and what the record holds, and let the reader see the fusion; the word 'rumour' is off the headline. (3) Stage 2's religious flag asked the cards to explain why Mossad narratives resonate with Muslim audiences; this is declined under the 3R rule (critique policy, not communities). Palestine appears only where the record puts it: Anwar's own stated reason and the BRN's video. (4) Stage 2's gender flag on the Selangor couple is moot: the couple is off the cards. Compression decisions: the Pai tourist-police debunk, the 2022 abduction, the Phuket Chabad inspection and the Meta reports are off the cards for length and primary-source reasons; all remain in the brief. 'Border plans' compresses 'principal plans for addressing southern-border unrest' and is a fair description of the Parliamentary Research Office's category, which includes development spending.
confidence: High on every card specific: each traces to a named primary or official-statement source listed in the brief's A-series (A33–A41 added at this stage). The absence finding is stated as bounded ('no case we checked'). Medium only on the reframe's characterisation of the conflict's cause, which rests on Crisis Group 2017 and the BRN spokesman's 2026 interview rather than a single document.
